name: Clean Architecture
description: Enforce clean/hexagonal architecture layer boundaries and dependency direction

rules.name: Domain Must Not Import Infrastructure
rules.description: The domain layer must never depend on infrastructure. Dependencies must point inward: infrastructure depends on domain, never the reverse. This is the fundamental rule of clean architecture.

config.message: Domain layer component must not depend on infrastructure. Invert the dependency using an interface.

rules.name: Use Cases Must Not Import Presentation
rules.description: Use cases (application layer) must not depend on presentation, handlers, or controllers. The application layer orchestrates domain logic and must remain agnostic to delivery mechanisms.

config.message: Use case must not import from the presentation layer. Use cases should be invoked by handlers, not depend on them.

rules.name: Adapters Must Implement Domain Ports
rules.description: Infrastructure adapters must implement domain-defined interfaces (ports). This ensures the domain remains decoupled from specific implementations.

config.message: Infrastructure adapter must implement a domain port (interface). Define the interface in the domain layer.

rules.name: No Framework Imports in Domain
rules.description: Domain layer must not use framework-specific technologies. The domain should be pure business logic, testable without any framework overhead.

config.message: Domain layer must not depend on framework technologies. Keep domain logic framework-agnostic.

rules.name: Entities Must Not Depend on External Services
rules.description: Domain entities must be self-contained. They must not hold references to external services, HTTP clients, or infrastructure components.

config.message: Entity must not depend on external services. Use a domain service or use case to coordinate external interactions.

rules.name: Repository Interfaces in Domain Layer
rules.description: Repository interfaces (ports) must be defined in the domain layer, not in infrastructure. This allows the domain to declare its data access needs without knowing the implementation.

config.message: Repository interface must be defined in the domain layer, not infrastructure.

rules.name: No Direct HTTP Calls From Domain
rules.description: Domain layer must not make HTTP calls directly. External communication must be abstracted behind a port (interface) and implemented in the infrastructure layer.

config.message: Domain layer must not use HTTP/network technologies directly. Define a port and implement it in the infrastructure layer.

rules.name: Handlers Must Only Call Use Cases
rules.description: Controllers and handlers in the presentation layer must only interact with use cases (application layer), never with repositories or infrastructure directly. This preserves the layered dependency flow.

config.message: Handler must only call use cases. Direct access to repositories or infrastructure from handlers breaks the architecture.

rules.name: Layered Container Structure
rules.description: Each service container must have clearly separated layers: at minimum a domain layer and an infrastructure layer, ensuring the architecture is consistently structured.

config.message: Container must have components tagged with both 'domain' and 'infrastructure' layers.
